summary: Lady Juliana disguises herself as a maid with Prudence to enter Ashbury Manor (spelled Ashburton once in E9; treated as the same location) and reaches the Dowager Duchess's bedchamber in the West Wing. On screen she finds the Duchess gravely ill and says 'This isn't ordinary fever' (EP22:E75), then asks who has been treating her (EP22:E79). Uncertainty: source coverage is incomplete for sc_001 and sc_002 and gaps are unavailable; source warning 'Line 102: Event interval outside scene' is unresolved and its affected event is not identified; E9 dialogue is cut off mid-sentence; 'Julian' (EP22:E27, housekeeper's address) is treated as an alias for Lady Juliana; 'Toby' (EP22:E13) and Lady Catherine/Lord Rupert (EP22:E9) appear only as mentions. Metadata (logline and continuity notes) is not on-screen evidence and is not used for claims here; it describes the illness as poisoned and says Episode 21 revealed the Duchess is dying, which is not verified on screen. Poisoning is not explicitly confirmed on screen; E80 only describes 'the haunting realization of poison' in a camera note.

beats.description: Juliana and Prudence stand in the service courtyard; Prudence warns of the watchful staff and Juliana insists the Duchess is dying and that she must act, then they enter the servant door.
The Housekeeper questions and tests the disguised Juliana, who answers meekly and is hired for work, with a warning against eyes and ears wandering.
After the Housekeeper leaves, Prudence expresses relief and Juliana asks for the West Wing; Prudence points toward the grand staircase and warns few servants go there.
Juliana crosses the grand hall, is awed by the portrait of the late Duke and Duchess, and Prudence urges her to keep moving toward the West Wing.
Juliana checks the empty hallway, enters the Duchess's bedchamber, and locks the door behind her, finding a frail figure in the bed with labored breathing.
Juliana addresses the Duchess, examines her pulse, and realizes the illness is not an ordinary fever.
The Duchess convulses and gasps; Juliana demands to know who has been treating her, and the episode ends on a suspenseful music cue as the Duchess chokes for air.
